subsystems.name: Quantum source
subsystems.role: generates the quantum states that carry the key — either very weak laser pulses or entangled photon pairs.

subsystems.name: Quantum channel
subsystems.role: transmits single photons from sender to receiver with as little loss and disturbance as possible.
parts: low-loss optical fibre (telecom wavelengths near 1550 nm)

subsystems.name: Single-photon detectors
subsystems.role: register individual photons arriving at the receiver.

subsystems.name: Classical channel
subsystems.role: carries the public discussion needed to turn raw detections into a shared secret key.
parts: authenticated encryption to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks

subsystems.name: Post-processing unit
subsystems.role: converts noisy detection events into a shorter, provably secret key.

subsystems.name: Range extenders
subsystems.role: bridge distances beyond what a single direct link can cover.
parts: trusted nodes that store and relay keys

buildSteps.title: Choose the protocol and platform
buildSteps.detail: Decide between prepare-and-measure schemes (e.g. BB84) or entanglement-based schemes (e.g. E91), and whether the link will be fibre, free-space, or satellite.

buildSteps.title: Build the transmitter
buildSteps.detail: Assemble a laser, modulator and attenuator to produce weak coherent pulses, or a nonlinear crystal to generate entangled photon pairs. Align optics to sub-micron precision.

buildSteps.title: Install the quantum channel
buildSteps.detail: Lay optical fibre with low loss and controlled polarisation, or set up a telescope for free-space links. Keep the channel as short as practical because loss rises exponentially with distance.

buildSteps.title: Set up detection
buildSteps.detail: Mount single-photon detectors, cool them to reduce noise, and connect fast timing electronics to record arrival times.

buildSteps.title: Implement the classical channel
buildSteps.detail: Establish a conventional network link for basis reconciliation, error correction and authentication. Synchronise clocks to nanosecond accuracy.

buildSteps.title: Develop post-processing software
buildSteps.detail: Write software to sift raw bits, correct errors, and apply privacy amplification to distill a shorter key whose secrecy is guaranteed by quantum mechanics.

buildSteps.title: Integrate with encryption
buildSteps.detail: Feed the distilled key into a one-time pad or a symmetric cipher, and link it to the application that needs secure communication.

buildSteps.title: Test and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Measure the quantum bit error rate, secure key rate and maximum distance. Verify that any eavesdropping attempt raises the error rate detectably.

prerequisites.why: the key is encoded in individual photons, so they must be emitted and detected reliably.
fibre spans of tens to a few hundred kilometres are needed for realistic metro and intercity links.
entanglement-based protocols offer stronger security proofs but are harder to build and scale.
without them, key rates fall to zero beyond a few hundred kilometres of fibre.
interoperability and security evaluation are still maturing, which slows wide deployment.

pathway.milestone: point-to-point QKD links in metro networks and dedicated fibre
pathway.unlocks: information-theoretically secure key exchange over short distances for banks, data centres and government users.

pathway.milestone: satellite QKD and trusted-node networks spanning cities
pathway.unlocks: intercity and intercontinental key distribution, as demonstrated by the Micius satellite.

pathway.milestone: quantum repeaters that extend entanglement over long fibre
pathway.unlocks: direct quantum links without trusted intermediate nodes.

pathway.milestone: a quantum internet linking many nodes
pathway.unlocks: end-to-end quantum-secure communication, distributed quantum computing and sensing.
